Check if the log level is set to a given level name, or higher.

## Signature

```typescript
isLevel(level: LogLevel): boolean;
```

## Parameters

<table><thead><tr><th>

Parameter


</th><th>

Type


</th><th>

</th></tr></thead>
<tbody><tr><td>

level


</td><td>

[LogLevel](/logger-ts/docs/api/logger/typealiases/loglevel)


</td><td>

The name of the log level.


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

## Returns

boolean

True if the current log level is equal to the given  level or higher.

## Exceptions

A `TypeError` if the level is not a string.

A `RangeError` if the level is not one of the valid names.

## Remarks

This is a more generic version of the accessors (like `isDebug`<!-- -->), to be used when the log level is not known at compile time.

Before a level is set (the preliminary state), it returns `true` for every level, so that the messages produced under the check are buffered rather than lost; they are filtered when the level is set. Use `hasLevel` to tell whether a level was set.

It can also be used to ensure that the log level is not decreased. Since in the preliminary state there is no level to compare with, check `hasLevel` first:

- added in v6.0.0

## Example


```javascript
if (!log.hasLevel || !log.isLevel(newLevel)) {
  log.level = newLevel
}
```
